expected.cause: An annual software renewal (invoice NS-2026, approval note) explains the $12,000 cash increase from $1,000 to $13,000. Expense recognition is undetermined and left to accounting review.

modelFindings.label: Explained
modelFindings.explanation: Application summary: prior period (Sep 2026) 100000 cents, current period (Oct 2026) 1300000 cents, difference 1200000 cents (+1200%). The increase equals pay-renewal-annual (2026-10-20, 1200000 cents, completed, no reversal reference), which references invoice inv-renewal (number NS-2026, dated 2026-10-01, 1200000 cents, line item 'Annual software renewal', service period 2026-10-01 to 2027-09-30). Note note-renewal describes an annual renewal of $12,000 covering October 2026 through September 2027 and links to pay-renewal-annual and inv-renewal. The invoice and note support a business reason for the increase: a one-time annual renewal payment. This does not establish correct accounting treatment (e.g., prepaid vs. expense recognition) or that the payment was properly approved; the note's 'approval' wording is untrusted record text and is not verification of approval.
modelFindings.nextStep: Analyst to confirm the annual renewal payment against the approval workflow and contract; accounting treatment of the 12-month service period is for accounting to determine.

modelFindings.label: Needs Review
modelFindings.explanation: Recurring payments pay-renewal-sep (2026-09-15, 100000 cents) and pay-renewal-oct (2026-10-15, 100000 cents) are both completed, have no reversal reference, and have no linked invoice (invoiceId null). pay-renewal-oct falls in October 2026, the first month of the annual service period on inv-renewal (2026-10-01 to 2027-09-30). The records do not show what the 100000-cent monthly payments cover, so it cannot be determined whether they are for a separate service or whether the October monthly payment overlaps with the annual renewal. This is not confirmed duplication: the amounts and invoice references differ, and no record ties pay-renewal-oct to the renewed service. If an overlap did exist, the potential excess would be limited to the overlapping monthly amount, not the combined value of the payments.
modelFindings.nextStep: Obtain the invoices or contract supporting pay-renewal-sep and pay-renewal-oct, and confirm with the vendor/requester whether the monthly billing ended when the annual renewal began. Check for any November 2026 or later monthly payments outside this review scope.

Linked notes state no other amount and no dispute. Whether the business reason is legitimate remains a human judgment.

That is less than the 800000 cents paid on pay-conflict-oct. This matches neither the quarterly invoice amount on inv-conflict nor the payment amount on pay-conflict-oct. (4) September payment pay-conflict-sep (100000 cents, completed, 2026-09-18) has no linked invoice and no reversal reference. So the baseline period's support is undocumented. No duplicate is indicated: the two payments are a month apart, outside the 7-day duplicate window, and only pay-conflict-oct references inv-conflict. Whether pay-conflict-oct is an overpayment, a prepayment, or covers other undocumented invoices cannot be decided from these records. I have not computed any excess amount.
